extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, education policymakers, and philosophers of education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative principles for organizing schooling in democratic societies, emphasizing the vocational dimension, integration of activity and thought, and the philosophical dispositions education should cultivate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of school and out-of-school apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: The out-of-school phase of education (apprenticeship) supplements the narrow and formal character of school work; school training should be part of apprenticeship to a calling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: School and experiential/apprenticeship learning should be coordinated so that formal instruction complements practical, on-the-job training rather than being isolated; treat schooling as part of continuous formation for a vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that higher education has vocational character
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher institutions of learning have often been, consciously or unconsciously, preparatory for pursuits of ruling, leadership, teaching, and research—i.e., they prepare for specific callings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating 'liberal' or 'cultural' education as non-vocational in practice; acknowledge that training for authorship, teaching, leadership, or research is vocational and should be designed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic esteem for manual labor and service
rubrics_metrics.description: In democratic communities there is increased esteem for manual labor, commercial occupations, and rendering tangible services; citizens are expected to contribute in return for social support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and pedagogy should respect and valorize manual and service occupations, embedding in students the ethic of service and social responsibility rather than maintaining aristocratic prejudices against such work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum responsiveness to industrial/commercial change
rubrics_metrics.description: The world-wide growth of manufacturing and commerce requires schools to relate more explicitly to industrial life and address social readjustment problems tied to capital and labor relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational programs should be revised to address modern industrial realities — not by reproducing them, but by preparing students to understand and act within them (economics, organization, social implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of scientific and technological content in vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry is now technological—based on discoveries in mathematics, physics, chemistry, bacteriology, etc.—so vocational education must acquaint workers with the scientific bases and social bearings of their pursuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid narrow rule-of-thumb/trade-only instruction; provide scientific and theoretical foundations that enable workers to understand and adapt to technological systems rather than becoming mere appendages to machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of laboratory and shop as complementary educational settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory work allows following up intellectual interests; shop work emphasizes the social bearings of principles. Their separation is largely conventional and each has distinct educative advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design programs that integrate hands-on shop experience with laboratory inquiry so students gain both insight into how knowledge is produced and an appreciation of its social application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychology-informed progression from play to work
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern psychology emphasizes instincts of exploring and experimentation; for older pupils, work serves the educative function that play serves for younger pupils; the passage from play to work should be gradual and preserve elements of play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure vocational tasks to retain exploratory and playful elements, enabling progressive reorganization of activities toward greater control and responsibility rather than abrupt adult-like labor expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of school materials and methods around occupations
rubrics_metrics.description: School materials and methods should be gradually reconstructed to utilize forms of occupation typifying social callings, bringing out their intellectual and moral content and relegating purely literary/dialectical methods to auxiliary roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize activity-centered curricula that use occupationally-relevant problems and projects as organizing centers of study; treat textbooks/dialectical exercises as supports, not the core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of narrow trade education that perpetuates class divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocational education that simply provides technical efficiency for jobs as they now operate risks perpetuating social predestination, hardening divisions between liberal/cultural education for the few and trade training for the many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject programs that track disadvantaged youth into narrowly instrumental trade training without broader intellectual, civic, and historical context; assess whether vocational programs reproduce existing social hierarchies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full intellectual and social meaning of a vocation in curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: A true vocational education includes instruction in historic background, training in science to give intelligence and initiative, and study of economics, civics, and politics to connect workers with social problems and methods for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design vocational courses to include: historical context of the industry, scientific principles underlying the work, and civic/economic education so trainees can understand and influence the social conditions of their labor; emphasize readaptation skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for adaptability and readaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocational education should train the power of readaptation to changing conditions so future workers will not become blindly subject to a fate imposed upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include problem-solving, general scientific principles, and flexible skills that allow workers to adjust to technological and economic change rather than narrowly optimized task skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education to develop capacity for shared social control
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should give workers desire and ability to share in social control, enable them to master their industrial fate, and to saturate technical and mechanical features with social meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure programs by whether they foster civic agency, collective competence, and critical understanding of social institutions, not merely technical mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'vocation' as educative target
rubrics_metrics.description: A vocation signifies any form of continuous activity which renders service to others and engages personal powers in behalf of the accomplishment of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this broad definition to design curricula: any sustained service-oriented activity can be educationally formative, not just traditional professions or trades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as renewal/transmission for social continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is the process by which social groups maintain continuous existence: renewal of meanings of experience through transmission, both incidental (companionship) and deliberate (institutions), involving growth of individual and group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate educational proposals by their capacity to renew social meanings and transmit civic commitments, balancing incidental socialization with deliberate curricular aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic criterion: continuous reconstruction of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal for democratic education is continuous reconstruction or reorganization of experience to increase social content and the capacity of individuals to act as directive guardians of this reorganization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and methods should foster ongoing critical reexamination of experience, emphasize social relevance of subject matter, and prepare learners to participate in reforming social institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of method and subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Method in study is the consciously directed movement of reorganization of the subject matter of experience; unity of method and subject matter is essential to democratic education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor pedagogies where subject matter is learned through methods that reflect its social purpose—e.g., problem-based, inquiry-driven learning that reorganizes experience rather than rote reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic disposition: totality, continuity, and generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy as educative aim denotes a disposition toward totality (continuity of response across diverse events), generality (placing acts in context), and ultimateness (penetrating to deeper levels of meaning); it is calm, open-minded, and able to learn from adversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess education by whether it cultivates habits of reflective, integrative thinking and a disposition to seek deeper connections rather than fragmentary or dogmatic learning; emphasize continuity rather than isolated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate thinking (philosophy) not merely knowledge (science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy differs from science: knowledge is settled facts; philosophy is thinking—prospective, hypothetical, concerned with what the known demands of us. Education should form dispositions to think and act, not merely store scientific facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design programs that develop the habit of reflective inquiry and moral/intellectual judgment; value hypothetical problem-posing and testing over mere memorization of settled knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrative approach to reconcile conflicting interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Education (and philosophy) must enable integration of conflicting interests—scientific, religious, economic, aesthetic, institutional vs individuality—especially where conflicts affect the community as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use curricula that present multiple perspectives, encourage critical negotiation among values, and prepare students for public deliberation and communal problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalize philosophy through educative conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophic ideas must take effect in conduct; public agitation, legislation, and administration are effective only insofar as they are educative and modify mental and moral attitudes; schooling must be animated by philosophical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge reforms and policies by whether they are educative in practice—i.e., do they change dispositions and conduct over time? Avoid purely rhetorical or dogmatic initiatives that lack educative mechanisms.
